text: Keep the resume to 1 page (up to 2 for 10+ years of experience). Recruiters spend about 6-10 seconds on a first scan.
Start with a 2-3 line professional summary tailored to the target role, mentioning your key skills and strongest achievement.
Quantify achievements with numbers and percentages, e.g. 'Reduced API latency by 40%' instead of 'Improved performance'.
Begin each bullet with a strong action verb (Built, Designed, Led, Optimized, Automated) rather than 'Responsible for'.
Include a Projects section with 2-3 relevant projects, a short description, the tech stack and a GitHub link.
Add links to your GitHub and LinkedIn profiles so recruiters can verify your work.
Put an email address and phone number at the top of the resume, using a professional email address.
Mirror keywords from the job description (skills, tools) so Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) rank the resume higher.
Use a clean single-column layout, standard section headings (Experience, Education, Skills) and a readable font; avoid images and tables that ATS cannot parse.
List education with degree, institution and graduation year; add GPA only if it is strong.
